The “Summer of Our Discontent” by Thomas Chatterton Williams confronts the breakdown of civility in America. Join Williams for a discussion with Cato’s Erec Smith about the existential crisis facing American liberalism, and how we might move beyond the current impasse toward a more integrated and resilient public square.

Register to attend in person or watch live: ow.ly/Y37b50YYXxc

President Trump's fertility treatment proposal would cut some regulations and save some workers money—but it's not much of a win for liberty or consumer sovereignty, says Cato's @mfcannon. 

For every $1 of tax savings, workers must surrender control of $3 of their earnings to their employer.

Can dollarization play a key role in achieving stability and growth in Latin America? 

Join Cato for a discussion featuring @VasquezIan, @JohnHCochrane, @DavidRMalpass, and @ocampo_emilio — exploring the mechanics of dollarization and why this reform is especially relevant to Argentina and Venezuela today.

Register to attend in person or watch live: ow.ly/Ourg50YZ0Sv

Juries are a final check on government overreach. But a bill from Rep. Letlow would defund juror education, keeping jurors unaware of their power to shield neighbors from unjust laws.

ow.ly/weiJ50YYmXI

Government prosecutors often fail crime victims. Reviving private prosecutions—an American tradition—would give victims real options, not a state monopoly.

Banks file 28.7 million reports on customers every year, at a cost of $59 billion. But only about 275 criminal investigations are started. That's a 0.02% success rate. The Bank Secrecy Act isn't fighting crime — it's spying on you without a warrant. Time to end it, says Cato’s @EconWithNick.

ow.ly/IY0950YYlq1

A president can violate the Constitution in two ways: by taking powers he doesn’t have or by abusing powers he does. The second is harder to stop. Courts struggle to police it, so Congress and voters must step up, says Cato’s Molly Nixon. 
ow.ly/QBNP50YXNPp

States that allowed bank branching by 1940 saw lasting manufacturing gains, as branches moved capital to underserved areas. Deregulation works.

ow.ly/EVoH50YYiKx

Across much of the United States, gas and electricity prices are rising, with little relief in sight. But there is a way to improve energy affordability. The Cato Institute’s @ts_fisher lays out what federal and state policymakers can do to bring energy costs down.
 
Check out the Cato Institute Handbook on Affordability:

Psychiatrists once used therapy, now most just manage medications. When the system rewards prescribing over talking, practices change, explains Cato’s Jeffrey A. Singer, MD.

ow.ly/SN0i50YXQs6

A free, open, and civil society depends on the freedom of individuals and institutions to direct private resources toward the causes they value. Today, that freedom faces growing pressure as the federal government seeks to use nonprofit status as a lever of political control. 

Join us for a conversation with President and CEO of DonorsTrust Lawson Bader, Cato Senior Fellow Walter Olson, and President of the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation John Palfrey on the importance of philanth

FEMA's cost-sharing rewards risk and waste. Real reform means shifting disaster costs to states and the private sector, where incentives align with risk, argues Cato’s @LettDominik.

What if you could design your own job—and get paid to do it? The Cato Innovation Project creates two-year paid positions at the Cato Institute.  

🔹 You design and propose your own full-time paid job to advance the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace.  

🔹 Cato decides whether to fund it by hiring you.  

Apply now: ow.ly/QRFk50YXJRt
